newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen hugging 21,000 range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen hugging 21,000 range.

text.p: Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 is likely to hug the 21,000 level in this week as it searches for a chance to break free of its recent range, market sources said.
"The floor is firming, as interest rates are not likely to be raised soon and pension funds are eager to buy on dips," said Haruo Nakaharu, strategist at Toyo Securities.
"But unless the index can keep its head up above the end-March level of 21,406, it may not have the strength to break out of that box," he added.
On Friday, the Nikkei 225 settled 15.18 points or 0.07 percent lower at 21,020.36. On November 22, it closed at 21,216.11.
Brokers said that the market still lacked motivation to fuel buying across the board, despite the recent frenzy of activity in certain global issues such as Honda Motor Co Ltd.
The blue-chip rally should resume next week after foreign investors return from the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday, said Harushige Kobayashi, Yamaichi Securities deputy general manager.
The November report on U.S. non-farm payrolls, often seen as the most crucial set of data each month, is due on Friday.
"What is worrying is the staggering number of issues falling to yearly lows behind the surging blue chips," Kobayashi said.
"Unless they peak out, gains will be hard to accumulate."
Brokers added that blue-chip demand had yet to expand and the future strength of the market depended greatly upon it.
Hopes of renewed interest in debutantes were pinned on the listing of Nippon Broadcasting System Inc, due to go public on December 2.
"Recently, newly listed stock have gotten off to bad starts, falling below the initial offer price," a "big four" trader said.
"If Nippon Broadcasting does well, it may break the trend."

Brokers added that with the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey on business sentiment out, the upcoming expiry of the December Nikkei 225 futures and options, called the special quotations (SQ), was the next item of interest.
"It depends on how smoothly the rollover goes but the market will be sensitive next week to arbitrage-linked trade and futures positions," a "Big Four" brokerage broker said.
